Internal helper: the news an update brings, ready to print

Source: R/utils.R
dot-jst_update_news.Rd

After a successful update, jupdate() prints the entries of the NEWS.md the new version installed, for the versions newer than the one the session had, so a tester who updates sees what changed without visiting the release page (Capability Slate C4, Session 379; Jeff, S378: "we can have jupdate print the news file - at least until the time right when I'm going to submit to CRAN, at which point it can be re-evaluated."). R installs a package's NEWS.md at the top of its folder in the library, from a source package and in a binary alike (observed on R 4.3.3, S379), so the file is read from the library the update went into – never the loaded copy, which is the old version – as .jst_update_installed_version() reads the version.

Usage

.jst_update_news(lib, from, to)

Arguments

lib

The library folder the update was installed into.

from

The version the session had before the update.

to

The version now installed.

Value

Character(1): "", or the lead line, the entries newest first and a closing blank line, to be spliced into jupdate()'s message.

Details

Nothing here can cost the user the update: a file that is missing or unreadable, or that holds no entry newer than from, gives "", and jupdate()'s success message prints as it always has. A file that cannot be opened makes readLines() WARN before it errors (as an address that cannot be read does, Session 340), so a warning is caught as an error is and gives "" – otherwise R's "cannot open file" would print under a successful update (found by startup_check.R I08).
